title: useContext finally clicked for me
content: Spent the weekend refactoring my to-do app so I could stop passing props through four layers. Context felt like overkill until I counted how many components were only forwarding `user`. Now it is one provider and the tree is so much cleaner.

title: A quiet seat during end-sem week
content: If you are hunting for a calm spot to study: the third-floor reading room opens at 7:30 and almost nobody is there before 9. Bring a charger, the sockets by the windows work.

title: What the aptitude round actually had
content: Sat through two company aptitude rounds this week. Mostly time-speed-distance, a few puzzles, and one data-interpretation set that ate twelve minutes. Practise DI under a timer. It is the section that surprises people.

title: Golden hour at the east gate
content: Shot with the kit lens at f/5.6, 1/250. Learned the hard way that exposing for the sky and lifting the shadows later beats the other way round. Any tips for keeping noise down at ISO 1600?

title: My first classifier, honestly reviewed
content: Built a tiny image classifier for three campus bird species. 71% accuracy, mostly because the dataset is 90 photos. Biggest lesson: better data beat every tweak I made to the model.

title: One more player for the esports night
content: We are putting together a 5v5 team for the inter-hostel esports night. Need one more player who is comfortable in a support role and does not mind scrims at 10 pm.

title: Talk to ten people before you write code
content: Interviewed twelve hostel residents about laundry pick-up before building anything. Nine of them said the same thing: the timing matters more than the price. So glad we asked first.

title: Open mic planning: who wants a slot?
content: Planning a small acoustic open mic at the amphitheatre next month. If you play, sing or do spoken word, drop a comment with how long you need. Sound equipment is sorted.

title: Short books for a long commute
content: Three reads that made the bus ride shorter this month: an essay collection about cities, a detective novel set in Kolkata, and a surprisingly funny book on statistics. What should I read next?

title: Linked list notes, redrawn as diagrams
content: Rewrote my data structures notes as pointer diagrams instead of paragraphs. Insert and delete suddenly became obvious. I can share how I structured them if that helps.

title: Grid or flexbox? My rule of thumb
content: Flexbox when the content decides the layout, grid when the layout decides where content goes. It is not perfect, but it stops me overthinking every component.

title: Hostel mess feedback on Friday
content: The student committee is collecting menu suggestions on Friday. Bring specific ideas. 'Make it tastier' is hard to act on, 'add a sprouts salad twice a week' is easy.

title: Resume checklist before you hit send
content: One page. Projects with numbers. No photo. Links that actually open. And a file name that is not resume_final_v7.pdf.

title: Day 21 of the pocket sketchbook
content: I carry a small sketchbook on the train now and draw whatever is in front of me for ten minutes. Three weeks in, my hands feel less stiff and I notice more.

title: Built it in plain JavaScript first
content: I wrote a small markdown notes app with only HTML, CSS and JavaScript, then rebuilt it in React. Seeing the same app as components made the benefit obvious in a way tutorials never did.

title: What do you listen to while debugging?
content: My debugging playlist is mostly instrumental film scores. Lyrics break my focus. What gets you through a bug that refuses to die?

title: A spreadsheet that calmed me down
content: Built a sheet that shows exactly what I need in the final exam to hit my target grade. Seeing one clear number was calmer than vague worry.

title: What should the freshers' guide include?
content: We are writing a guide for incoming first-years. Tell me one thing you wish you had known in your first week.

title: Reading group: attention, one section at a time
content: Starting a fortnightly reading group on transformer basics. No prerequisites except curiosity. We will read one paper section at a time and talk it through.

title: The internship email that got a reply
content: Three short paragraphs: who I am, one specific thing I liked about their product, and what I can contribute. I heard back in two days.

title: Pair programming hour is back
content: Open pair-programming hour in Lab 3 on Thursday evening. Bring a bug or an idea. Beginners are very welcome.

title: Photowalk this Saturday
content: Meeting at the main gate at 6:30 am for a campus photowalk. Phones are completely fine, no gear needed.

title: Retro game night results
content: We played old arcade classics in the common room and it got surprisingly competitive. Someone beat the high score on the snake clone I wrote last month 😅

title: Learning React Router, one route at a time
content: Moved my project from conditional rendering to real routes. Back and forward buttons just work now, and the URL actually tells you where you are.

title: Wi-Fi near the east block is flaky
content: Is anyone else losing connection near the east block after 8 pm? Trying to collect a few examples to send to the IT desk.
